title: Gran Turismo 7 Gets a Power Boost: Thrustmaster Unveils Next-Gen T-GT III Wheel
summary: Thrustmaster has unveiled the T-GT III Steering Wheel, marking a significant evolution in its 16-year partnership with Gran Turismo. Designed for PS4 and PS5, this new hardware promises unparalleled immersion for Gran Turismo 7 players with its innovative Direct Axial Drive system.
content:
For dedicated sim racers, the quest for ultimate immersion is an unending journey. Every nuance of the track, every shift in weight, and the precise feel of a car's grip contributes to that elusive sense of reality. Now, Thrustmaster is raising the stakes, ushering in what they're calling a “new era” for virtual driving with the announcement of their T-GT III Steering Wheel, tailor-made for Gran Turismo 7 on PS4 and PS5.

This isn't just another peripheral; it's a statement. Building on an impressive 16-year collaboration with the iconic Gran Turismo franchise, the T-GT III arrives with a groundbreaking Direct Axial Drive bundle. For the uninitiated, direct drive systems are the holy grail of force feedback, connecting the wheel directly to the motor without intermediate gears or belts. This translates to incredibly crisp, latency-free feedback, letting players feel every curb, every tire slip, and every subtle vibration with unprecedented fidelity.

The T-GT III isn't just about raw power; it's about precision. The direct drive mechanism significantly enhances the realism of Gran Turismo 7's physics engine, allowing players to react faster and more intuitively to what the car is doing on the virtual tarmac. Whether you're navigating the tight chicanes of the Nürburgring or power-sliding through the bends of Trial Mountain, the T-GT III promises an experience that blurs the lines between simulation and reality.

This latest offering underscores Thrustmaster's commitment to pushing the boundaries of licensed racing hardware. With the T-GT III, they're not just providing a new input device; they're inviting Gran Turismo fans to experience their favorite tracks and vehicles with a level of detail and responsiveness previously only dreamed of. Get ready to feel the road like never before.
keyTakeaways: Thrustmaster has launched the T-GT III Steering Wheel for PS4 and PS5, optimized for Gran Turismo 7.
The T-GT III introduces a Direct Axial Drive bundle, significantly enhancing force feedback realism and immersion.
This new hardware continues Thrustmaster's robust 16-year partnership with Gran Turismo, signaling a 'new era' for officially licensed racing peripherals.
author: Demi Williams

title: Crypto Keeper Emerges: Tonkeeper's Evolution Towards a Multi-Chain Self-Custody Future
summary: The Crypto Keeper wallet, formerly known as Tonkeeper, has undergone a significant transformation, evolving into a robust self-custodial solution that now supports an array of blockchain networks. This upgrade empowers users with direct control over their digital assets by storing private keys securely on their own devices, moving beyond its original TON network confines.
content:
The world of cryptocurrency wallets is constantly evolving, and a recent major player has just stepped into a broader spotlight. Say goodbye to Tonkeeper and welcome Crypto Keeper, a name change that signifies far more than just a rebrand. This isn't merely a fresh coat of paint; it's a strategic evolution designed to usher in a new era of self-custody for digital asset holders across a multitude of networks.

At its heart, Crypto Keeper remains steadfastly a self-custodial wallet. This critical distinction means users, and *only* users, hold the keys to their crypto kingdom, with private keys securely stored directly on their personal devices. This philosophy champions user autonomy and significantly reduces reliance on third-party custodians, mitigating risks associated with centralized hacks or censorship. What sets Crypto Keeper apart now is its dramatic expansion beyond the confines of the TON network. Initially tailored for The Open Network, it has ingeniously adapted its robust architecture to embrace additional blockchain ecosystems.

This multi-chain leap is a game-changer for anyone navigating the increasingly complex web3 landscape. Instead of juggling multiple, network-specific wallets, users can now consolidate their holdings and manage diverse digital assets from a single, trusted interface. This simplifies portfolio management, streamlines transactions, and enhances the overall user experience without compromising the bedrock principle of self-sovereignty. It's a clear response to the fragmented nature of the blockchain world, offering a streamlined yet powerful tool for sophisticated crypto users and newcomers alike.

Crypto Keeper represents a thoughtful step forward in wallet technology. By combining its proven self-custodial security with expansive multi-chain support, it positions itself as a formidable contender for users who prioritize control, security, and convenience in their digital asset journey. Its journey from a specialized TON wallet to a versatile multi-chain solution underscores a growing trend towards more integrated, user-centric tools in the decentralized finance space.
keyTakeaways: Crypto Keeper is the new identity for the self-custodial wallet formerly known as Tonkeeper.
The wallet has evolved to support multiple blockchain networks, moving beyond its original focus on the TON network.
It prioritizes user autonomy and security by storing private keys directly on the user's device, ensuring self-custody.
author: Yevheny Serhiienko

title: AI's Secret Weapon? The Rise of the Forward-Deployed Engineer
summary: The tech industry is increasingly turning to "forward-deployed engineers," an embedded model popularized by firms like Palantir, to accelerate the integration of complex new technologies. While the idea of on-site experts isn't entirely new, this hands-on approach is proving exceptionally effective for companies navigating the rapid advancements of artificial intelligence.
content:
“Another day, another piece of tech jargon,” jokes Ryan Sheehan, a senior vice president at global solutions integrator SHI. His latest chuckle? The term “forward-deployed engineers.” Yet, beneath the industry’s penchant for new buzzwords lies a genuinely impactful trend, one that companies like Palantir have championed and which is now proving crucial in the frenetic race to adopt artificial intelligence.

These aren't your typical consultants parachuting in for a high-level strategy session. Forward-deployed engineers integrate deeply, becoming temporary but essential members of a client’s team. They're on the ground, rolling up their sleeves, often coding alongside internal staff, debugging systems, and directly implementing new software. The goal is rapid knowledge transfer and immediate operationalization, bypassing the often-slow adoption cycles.

The concept of embedded technical expertise isn't entirely novel, but its current surge reflects the urgent demands of the AI era. Companies are desperate to leverage advanced AI models but often lack the in-house expertise to integrate them effectively into legacy systems or complex workflows. Forward-deployed engineers bridge this gap, providing practical, hands-on guidance that accelerates deployment from months to mere weeks.

This model sidesteps traditional consulting's perceived distance, offering a more immediate, tactile transfer of capability. It's about showing, not just telling. For organizations struggling to keep pace with innovation, especially in AI and machine learning, having an expert literally embedded within their operational core can be the difference between groundbreaking success and costly stagnation. As the tech landscape continues its dizzying acceleration, expect to hear a lot more about these crucial, on-the-ground catalysts.
keyTakeaways: "Forward-deployed engineers" are embedded technical experts who work directly within client teams, rather than offering traditional, detached consulting.
This model, popularized by firms like Palantir, is experiencing a resurgence due to the urgent need for rapid AI integration and expertise.
By providing hands-on implementation and direct knowledge transfer, these engineers significantly accelerate the adoption of complex technologies, bridging internal skill gaps.
author: Simon Sharwood
